title: review: P0b: lifecycle stamps for time and token metrics — bus.create_task writes created_at; the gate stamps first_green_at once and counts gate attempts and reds; report_merge stamps accepted_at on the merged task and on its fix-round lineage root
spec:
Phase I P0 (brief .orchestrator/phase-i-program.md). Base goal/T-0445 after P0a (T-0449) merges. Scout facts: created_at is not a stored field, daemon derives it ad hoc from bus_events or file mtime (daemon.py:576-581); pipeline stamps are epoch floats written by daemon.stamp/complete (daemon.py:268-292): dispatched_at, spec_review_at, gated_at (daemon.gate, daemon.py:784-842 sets gated_at on success and holds on gate_red), review_held_at, merged_at via report_merge (daemon.py:847); fix-round lineage via constraints.fix_round_for and auto_round (daemon.py:139-201).
1. bus.create_task stores created_at = time.time() as a top-level task field (bus.py:101-125); bus.get keeps working for old tasks without it (readers treat absence as unknown, never crash).
2. daemon.gate: on every gate run increment pipeline.gate_attempts; on a red gate increment pipeline.gate_reds and keep the existing hold; on the first green set pipeline.first_green_at = time.time() only if absent (a later re-gate after rebase never moves it); when the gated task is a fix round (attribution.lineage(task).root != task id) also set first_green_at on the lineage root if absent, and always increment the root's pipeline.lineage_fix_rounds so first-pass success is decidable from the root alone (first pass = root has first_green_at, lineage_fix_rounds == 0 and gate_reds == 0). Use daemon.stamp/complete under the existing locking so concurrent stages keep their guarantees.
3. daemon.report_merge: on a successful merge set pipeline.accepted_at = the merge time on the merged task and, for a fix round, on its lineage root (which report_merge already marks merged_into); never overwrite an existing accepted_at.
4. Daemon.py's ad hoc created_at derivation (daemon.py:576-581) prefers the stored field when present.
Tests: tests/test_bus.py::test_create_task_sets_created_at, tests/test_daemon.py::test_gate_sets_first_green_once_and_counts_attempts, test_gate_red_increments_reds_and_keeps_hold, test_fix_round_gate_marks_root_first_green_and_lineage_count, test_report_merge_sets_accepted_at_on_task_and_root_without_overwrite, test_respawn_check_prefers_stored_created_at. Existing tests stay green; .claude/hooks/tests-green.sh exits 0; git add -A; commit with the task id; report sha and failures only.
acceptance: created_at, pipeline.first_green_at, gate_attempts, gate_reds, lineage_fix_rounds and accepted_at exist with the semantics above; old tasks without them never crash a reader
Existing tests pass; .claude/hooks/tests-green.sh exits 0 in the worktree

comments.issue: Acceptance requires new tests test_gate_sets_first_green_once_and_counts_attempts, test_gate_red_increments_reds_and_keeps_hold, test_fix_round_gate_marks_root_first_green_and_lineage_count, and (in tests/test_bus.py) test_create_task_sets_created_at and test_report_merge_sets_accepted_at_on_task_and_root_without_overwrite. None of these appear in the diff — only two pre-existing tests were touched (to pop created_at). The gate can't verify these acceptance-named tests because they don't exist yet.

gate_attempts is incremented unconditionally at the top of every gate() pass for any done/not-yet-gated execute task, before any real gate check (worktree existence, acceptance test check, or tests-green run) happens. Since gate() runs once per daemon tick (default interval=30s), a task merely waiting on its worktree will accumulate gate_attempts once per tick rather than once per actual attempt to validate it, inflating the counter independent of real gating work.
